gpui, gpui_wgpu, gpui_windows, gpui_macos and gpui_linux at zed 6b2aa1c90aeb72cadfd30ed12141ed9e2569eded, with the Riseonly patches.

Generated by scripts/vendor-gpui.py; never edit crates/, assets/ or Cargo.toml by hand: change
patches/*.diff and rerun the script (scripts/vendor-gpui.py --check says whether the tree is stale).

patches/0001-owned-nv12-surface.diff (P41, P27 lin): off macOS PaintSurface carries an
OwnedSurfaceFrame (NV12 planes in CPU memory, stream id, generation, YCbCr matrix), drawn through
gpui::surface(frame) or Window::paint_owned_surface. The wgpu renderer (Linux) uploads the planes
into per-stream R8 and RG8 textures when the generation changes and draws them with the surface
pipeline it already had (shaders.wgsl vs_surface/fs_surface). macOS (Metal) is unchanged.

patches/0002-windows-owned-surface.diff (P42, P27 win): the DirectX 11 renderer (Windows) draws
the same OwnedSurfaceFrame: per-stream R8 luma and R8G8 chroma textures, uploaded with
UpdateSubresource when the generation changes and released when the stream leaves the scene or
the device is lost, drawn by a new surface shader in shaders.hlsl (t2/t3, clamp sampler s1, the
frame's YCbCr matrix). build.rs compiles it with the other modules for release builds.

patches/0003-windows-external-drag.diff (P64): gpui_windows overrides can_start_external_drag and
start_external_drag. The paths are queued and the drag starts from a posted window message
(DoDragDrop is modal and must not run inside gpui's input dispatch) with SHDoDragDrop of an empty
SHCreateDataObject filled with CF_HDROP and the shell's default drop source; FileDropEvent::Ended
then closes the gpui drag, the same contract as the macOS dragging session (src/external_drag.rs).

patches/0005-macos-bgra-surface.diff (P148): the Metal renderer (gpui_macos) drew a PaintSurface
only from a full-range biplanar YCbCr (420f) CVPixelBuffer and asserted on anything else. A 32BGRA
CVPixelBuffer with premultiplied alpha is now bound as one BGRA8Unorm texture from the
CVMetalTextureCache and drawn by bgra_surface_fragment (shaders.metal) with the path sprite blending
(One, OneMinusSourceAlpha), so WebM stickers blend over what lies beneath. 420f is unchanged.

patches/0006-wgpu-bgra-surface.diff (P147): the wgpu renderer (Linux) draws OwnedSurfaceFrame::bgra
from one texture per BGRA stream in the colour atlas format (Bgra8Unorm, or Rgba8Unorm with a
red/blue swap in fs_surface), uploaded with Queue::write_texture on a new generation, sampled
without YCbCr and returned premultiplied, or straight when the pipeline blends straight alpha.

patches/0007-macos-scroll-cancelled.diff (A3-chat-005 mac): gpui_macos reported NSEventPhaseCancelled
of a scroll wheel event as TouchPhase::Moved, so two fingers that rested on the trackpad (MayBegin,
reported as Started) and lifted without scrolling left the gesture open forever: the chat list stayed
dragging. Cancelled is now TouchPhase::Cancelled; every other phase maps as before.

patches/0008-windows-shared-surface.diff (P149): on Windows OwnedSurfaceFrame::shared_nv12 carries a
SharedSurfaceHandle (an NT handle of an NV12 texture with a keyed mutex, plus a key) instead of CPU
planes, so a D3D11VA picture reaches the screen without a CPU copy. The DirectX 11 renderer opens
each handle once with ID3D11Device1::OpenSharedResource1, samples its planes through R8 and R8G8
shader resource views with the surface shader of patch 0002, holds the keyed mutex
(AcquireSync(0)/ReleaseSync(0)) around the draw and releases the opened textures when the handle
leaves the scene or after 240 scenes. Other platforms do not see the new variant.

patches/0009-linux-wayland-scroll-phases.diff (P195): gpui_linux sent every Wayland continuous scroll
as TouchPhase::Moved and ignored wl_pointer.axis_stop, so the two-finger back gesture (TouchPhase
Started/Moved/Ended over ScrollDelta::Pixels, as on macOS) never began on Linux. With
wl_pointer.axis_source finger the first scroll frame is now Started and the frame carrying
axis_stop, or a pointer leave in the middle of the scroll, sends ScrollWheel Pixels(0, 0) Ended.
Wheel and continuous sources stay Moved. X11 (XI2 smooth scroll arrives as lines without phases)
is unchanged: back there is Alt+Left and mouse button 8.

patches/0010-linux-clipboard-image.diff (P203): gpui_linux wrote only text to the system clipboard:
Wayland offered the text types and served text() for any type, X11 called set_text with the item's
text, so ClipboardItem::new_image left an empty string. Wayland now also offers the MIME type of the
item's first image and serves its bytes for that type (the text types stay offered when the item
has text or no image); X11 owns CLIPBOARD through set_image for an item with an image and no text,
under the atom of the image's own format (it was always image/png). Images go in one property
write: X11 has no INCR transfer on the owner side, so an image above the server's maximum request
length (BIG-REQUESTS, about 16 MB) is not carried. Reading the clipboard is unchanged.

patches/0011-transform-stack.diff (A2-core-ui-020): Window::with_transformation paints what its closure
paints through a matrix in scaled window pixels: quads and paths become transformed paths, glyphs and
svgs carry the matrix on their sprite, and the content mask active at the call clips all of it. Layout
and hit testing stay untransformed.

patches/0012-transformed-sprite-bounds.diff: Scene::insert_primitive culled and ordered sprites by
their bounds before the transformation while the shaders clip after it, so a turned sprite whose
unturned box left the mask vanished. Culling and draw order now use the transformed box.

patches/0013-transformed-images.diff (A2-core-ui-070): PolychromeSprite carries a transformation too,
so paint_image and paint_emoji turn, scale and mirror under with_transformation. The Metal, wgsl
(storage and webgl, stride 30 words) and hlsl shaders place the sprite through the matrix like a
monochrome one. The edge and corner distance is computed from an interpolated position in the sprite's
own space, not from the screen position, and scaled by the square root of the matrix determinant, so
rounded corners turn with the image. Shadows, underlines and surfaces stay untransformed.

patches/0014-public-glyph-raster.diff (A2-core-ui-041): TextSystem::raster_bounds and rasterize_glyph are public,
so PostTextLayout::make_bitmap rasterizes a caption off the frame as CoreText does on iOS.

patches/0015-windows-latin-binding-keys.diff (P220): on a non-Latin layout (Russian) MapVirtualKeyW names a
key in that layout, so "ctrl-v" and every binding never matched on Windows. A key named outside ASCII takes
its US layout name by virtual key, as guess_ascii does in gpui_linux; key_char keeps the typed text.

patches/0016-windows-scroll-end-on-lift.diff (P221): Direct Manipulation ended a trackpad scroll only in READY,
after the inertia, so every consumer read the inertia as fingers on the pad. Ended now comes on the switch to
INERTIA and the inertia follows as Moved with no second Ended, the macOS contract.

patches/0017-focus-handle-rendered.diff (X75): public FocusHandle::is_in_rendered_frame. A kit layer
that took the focus and returns it has to tell a remembered handle that still has an element from a
live handle whose element left the frame; focusing the latter would dispatch keys from the window root.

patches/0018-windows-session-end-quit.diff (P229): gpui_windows ignored WM_ENDSESSION, and Windows ends the
process right after it, so on_app_quit never ran on shutdown or sign-out. A top-level window now hands the
message to the platform window, which runs the quit callback once before returning.

patches/0020-windows-child-window-over-gpui.diff (P239): the DirectComposition target was topmost, so a child
window (WebView2 of a bot mini app) sat under every pixel gpui paints; it is now behind the children, the
same order as a subview over the gpui NSView. A mouse down on the window also takes the keyboard back from a
focused child, since the window is already active and Windows moves nothing.

patches/0019-linux-session-end-quit.diff (P230): gpui_linux left SIGTERM and SIGHUP at their default action, and
systemd ends a session with them, so on_app_quit never ran on log out or shutdown. The handler writes to a
pipe, a thread stops the event loop as Platform::quit does, and run() calls the quit callback. The handler goes
in after on_finish_launching: nothing needs saving during launch, and the default action still ends the process.
EventLoop::run clears the stop flag on entry, so the thread repeats the stop until the process exits.

patches/0021-surface-under-transformation.diff (X38): a video surface has no matrix in any renderer, so under
with_transformation it stayed at full size while the zoom push scaled the page around it. A matrix that only scales
and moves now maps the surface's box; a turn or a mirror keeps the untransformed box.

patches/0022-public-element-opacity.diff (A3-chat-071): Window::with_element_opacity is public, so a canvas
can fade what it paints itself; the removal dust of the chat list fades each of its image particles on its own.

Licensing: the five crates are Apache-2.0 (LICENSE-APACHE beside each). assets/fonts holds the two
SIL OFL 1.1 fonts their unit tests include, with their licence files. Every other zed crate stays
a git dependency of the same rev; no GPL zed source is copied here.

Used by the root Cargo.toml of the desktop through:
    [patch."https://github.com/zed-industries/zed"]
    gpui = { path = "vendor/gpui-6b2aa1c/crates/gpui" }
    gpui_wgpu = { path = "vendor/gpui-6b2aa1c/crates/gpui_wgpu" }
    gpui_windows = { path = "vendor/gpui-6b2aa1c/crates/gpui_windows" }
    gpui_macos = { path = "vendor/gpui-6b2aa1c/crates/gpui_macos" }
    gpui_linux = { path = "vendor/gpui-6b2aa1c/crates/gpui_linux" }

patches/0023-hyphen-line-break.diff (X385): LineWrapper::wrap_line also offers a break after a
hyphen followed by a letter, as Core Text does, so a long hyphenated file name in a two-line chat
preview wraps at its hyphens instead of leaving the leading glyph alone on the first line.
patches/0024-hyphen-shaped-wrap.diff (X385): LineLayout::compute_wrap_boundaries, the wrap that
shape_text really uses for a Text element, takes the same break after a hyphen as 0023.
patches/0025-shaped-end-truncation.diff (X562): a one-line Text that overflows and truncates from the
end is cut at its shaped glyph positions (LineWrapper::truncate_shaped_line_end) instead of summed
per-character advances, which run wider than the shaped line (no kerning) and left a gap between the
ellipsis and the next element (typing names before the verb in the chat header).

patches/0026-test-draws-per-flush.diff (X dev-drive hang 12.11): with test-support, flush_effects draws every
dirty window until no effects are left; a draw that leaves its window dirty (an animation notifying from
render) looped there forever and the dev-drive tester windows hung at 100% CPU. One flush now draws a window
at most MAX_TEST_DRAWS_PER_FLUSH (8) times; the rest waits for the next update. Builds without test-support
are unchanged.

patches/0027-rounded-surface-clip.diff (X767): a surface (video frame) ignored the corner radii of a
clipping container: the content mask is rectangular, so a video note drawn in
rounded_full().overflow_hidden() showed the square canvas around its circle. A Div with overflow
hidden and nonzero radii now paints its children inside Window::with_surface_corner_clip; PaintSurface
carries the innermost rounded box (corner_clip_bounds, corner_radii) and the Metal surface fragments
(420f and BGRA) multiply by the rounded box coverage (quad_sdf). wgpu and DirectX ignore the new fields.
patches/0028-frame-phase-timing.diff (X858, perf track): with frame tracing on (set_frame_trace_enabled),
FrameTiming also carries paint_start, paint_end and rendered_views, the count of view renders in the
frame (a reused cached view does not count); layout_duration (render, request_layout and prepaint) and
paint_duration split the draw. The marks live in a thread local and cost one atomic load with tracing off.
The desktop's RISE_PERF_LOG (app/src/app/perf/rise_perf_log.rs) reads them.

patches/0029-view-render-types.diff (X917, perf track): rendered_views now also counts entities embedded
as elements (Entity<T> through ViewElement), not only AnyView, and with tracing on every render adds to a
run total per Render type name; view_render_counts() returns the totals, the most rendered first. The
desktop's RISE_PERF_LOG writes the per-type deltas so a scenario shows which views render on each frame.

patches/0030-cached-view-stale-ranges.diff (X916, crash): a cached AnyView replays prepaint and paint by
index ranges into the previous frame. A view prepainted under a hidden div (Visibility::Hidden skips paint
of its children) or carried inside a replayed cached ancestor kept ranges of an older frame, and the next
replay sliced past the end (window.rs reuse_paint, range start 1201 out of range for slice of length 1106).
Window::draw_count numbers the frames; ViewElementState keeps the frame its prepaint and paint ranges came
from. Prepaint replays only ranges of the frame just before; a paint with an older range draws nothing and
notifies the view, which renders fresh in the next frame.

patches/0033-bracket-line-break.diff (X976): LineWrapper::wrap_line and LineLayout::compute_wrap_boundaries
no longer break before a closing bracket or ! ?, after an opening bracket, or between a letter and the
opening bracket after it (UAX #14 LB13, LB14, LB30): a chat preview ending in "joined(a) the chat" wrapped as
"joined(a" + ") the chat"; it now wraps at the space, as Core Text does.

patches/0034-parked-hidden-view-paint.diff (X1167, perf track): a cached view under a Visibility::Hidden div
replays its prepaint but is not painted, so its paint ranges went stale and the frame that showed it again
rendered it fresh (the desktop's tab switch: two full page renders, 52 ms). Div::prepaint now counts hidden
divs (Window::hidden_depth). A cached view prepainted under one takes the paint it recorded in the frame
just before out of that frame (ParkedPaint: scene operations, mouse listeners, cursor styles, tab stops,
the element states its paint reads, kept alive every hidden frame) and replays it when shown again with the
same cache key; input handlers stay behind (a hidden view holds no focus). A parked paint dies when any
image leaves the sprite atlas (Window::image_drops) or the view renders. Shown with no replayable paint the
view renders at prepaint instead of drawing nothing for a frame (the 0030 fallback stays for anything else).
Deferred draws under a hidden div are dropped (they paint at the window level over what is shown); a view
whose render dropped one renders again when shown, and a range holding deferred draws does not replay
under a hidden div.

patches/0035-nested-cached-view-reuse.diff (X1167, perf track): a cached view that rendered fresh set
Window::refreshing for its whole subtree, so every cached view nested in it rendered too. On the profile a
worn gift effect notifies each frame, its ancestors are dirty, and the two cached tab pages under the route
page rendered on every frame with all their rows (draw 9-10 ms at rest, layout 6-7 ms). A fresh render now
keeps the outer refreshing value: a nested cached view still renders when it is dirty, its cache key moved,
the window refreshes, or its ranges are not of the frame just before (0030 check), and replays otherwise.

patches/0036-env-fingerprint-cache-key.diff (X1167, perf track, review RW604): after 0035 a cached view under an
environment scope (rise-ui swiftui::environment::env_scope) replayed its old frame when only the scope's value
changed, because environment values live outside gpui and were neither in the cache key nor dirtied the view.
Window::env_fingerprint is a fingerprint of the environment values around the element being prepainted:
EnvScope::prepaint mixes its key and value into it for its children and restores it afterwards. The cached view
keeps it in ViewElementCacheKey next to bounds, content mask and text style, so a changed value above it renders
it fresh, as SwiftUI hands a new environment value to the whole subtree.

patches/0037-hidden-view-keeps-key.diff (X1167, perf track, bench 287 tabs max 53 ms): the kept tab pages sit
under hidden divs (app main_tabs offstage) with the centre's size, and the centre narrows or widens when a
section opens or closes the right panel, so every tab switch that moved the panel missed the cache key of every
hidden tab page and rendered and laid out all of them (the feed's rows included) in that frame. A cached view
under a hidden div (Window::hidden_depth, 0034) now replays its last prepaint whatever its key, and keeps the old
key: the frame that shows it again compares that key and renders it fresh only when bounds, mask, text style or
environment really moved. Dirty views, refreshing windows and stale ranges (0030) still render while hidden.

patches/0039-hidden-dirty-view-waits.diff (X1259, perf track, T5 b293 Reports p95 35 ms, layout 31 ms): a page
pushed over the tabs (Settings, Moderation, Reports) hides the root slot, but every notify of a store the feed
read made the hidden Posts view dirty, and 0037 still rendered dirty views while hidden: each frame of a tab
switch or the sort menu rendered and laid out the feed's rows (PostRowTextLineView 64-128 a frame) under the
page. A dirty cached view under a hidden div (Window::hidden_depth) now replays its last prepaint and marks its
state stale_while_hidden; can_replay refuses it once it is shown, so the frame that shows it again renders it
fresh. Refreshing windows, stale ranges (0030) and deferred draws still render while hidden.

patches/0040-focus-change-dirties-focus-path.diff (X1278, perf track, T2 b295 media picker preview p95 15.9 ms):
Window::focus and blur called refresh(), so every focus move rendered every cached view of the window: a click
on a picker tile focuses the editor host and then the editor root, and each of the two frames drew the chat
list, the chat with its wallpaper, the picker grid and the hidden feed (177-183 views, layout 11-13 ms). A
focus move now dirties only the views on the old and the new focus path (DispatchTree::focus_view_path,
WindowInvalidator::mark_views_dirty, no notify effect, so observe_self of RootView stays quiet); the same for
a focus move made by focus listeners at the end of a draw. A view that styles by a handle outside its own
subtree has to observe that handle's focus events itself.

patches/0041-moved-view-replay.diff (X1285 for X1277, perf track, T6 b295 profile Items grid scroll p95 57 ms,
GiftCosmeticSurfaceView 64 renders a frame): the cache key compares the whole bounds, so a scroll that only
moves every visible cached cell rendered, laid out and painted each of them again. A cached view opted in with
ViewElement::replay_when_moved that keeps its size, text style and environment, is clean, was painted in the
frame just before, moved by whole device pixels, and whose mask either moved along (a clipped cell) or stayed
and cut nothing it drew or hit-tests before and after (Window::ranges_clear_of_mask) now
replays its last prepaint and paint at the new origin: Window::reuse_moved_prepaint moves its hitboxes,
Scene::replay_moved moves primitives, clips, path vertices and sprite transformations. A view whose ranges hold
mouse listeners, input handlers, tooltips or deferred draws still renders (they keep the old origin). Prepaint
callbacks that read window positions register Window::on_replayed_move and get the offset from the bounds they
saw (rise-ui WindowScreenFrameReader); element states keep their old positions, hence opt-in.

patches/0042-hidden-view-skips-refresh.diff (X1299, perf track, T6 b295 Settings > Moderation p95 10-11 ms,
T7 Settings > Report p95 22 ms, PostRowTextLineView 87-224 renders under the hidden feed): 0039 let a dirty
cached view under a hidden div wait, but Window::refresh still rendered, laid out and prepainted every hidden
tab and stack page (the whole Posts feed) on each refresh a measuring element or a menu asks for. A cached view
under a hidden div now replays on a refreshing frame too and is marked stale_while_hidden, so the frame that
shows it again renders it fresh.

patches/0043-moved-replay-mask-offset.diff (X1285 review RW640): a 0041 move callback got only the view's
offset, so WindowScreenFrameReader moved its frame but kept the old clip; a cell scrolled whole together with
its clip (a horizontal shelf inside a vertical store page) read as clipped away after scrolling more than its
height and stopped playback. Window::on_replayed_move callbacks now also get how far the content mask around
them moved: the offset when the mask moved along, zero when the mask is the viewport that stayed.

patches/0044-moved-replay-mouse-listeners.diff (X1318, perf track, T7 b295 post comments in the right panel
p95 15 ms, CommentHostedRowView and CommentsSheetRowView rendered ~10 per frame while scrolling): 0041 refused a
moved replay for any range with mouse listeners, and every list row has them (like, reply, menu). A moved replay
now keeps them: the hitboxes move (0041), while the listeners and element states keep the old origin, so a view
with listeners renders whenever the mouse is over it before or after the move, and a view drawn with listeners
of an earlier origin (or holding such a view) is listed in Frame::moved_views; the mouse reaching one notifies
it, so it renders before what the mouse does next. Input handlers, tooltips and deferred draws still refuse.

patches/0045-nested-view-replay-rebase.diff (X1259 redo, perf track, T5 b305 Reports tab switch p95 11.3 ms, sort
menu 12.5 ms, PostRowTextLineView 112-224 renders under the hidden feed): a cached view that replays its prepaint
copies the prepaint of every cached view nested in it, but their states kept the ranges and frame of the render
that recorded them. The next frame that rendered the outer view (the navigation stack holding the hidden root slot
and the pushed Settings > Moderation > Reports page) found the nested hidden feed on an older frame (0030 check)
and rendered and laid it out with all its rows. Window::update_replayed_states hands the nested ViewElementStates
whose keys a replay copied to view.rs, and each one prepainted in the frame just before takes the range its
prepaint was copied to (PrepaintStateIndex::rebase_within, LineLayoutIndex::rebased) and this frame, and keeps its
parked paint alive. Paint ranges stay as they were, so a shown nested view still renders unless it replayed its own
paint; a moved replay (0041) and a stale hidden replay (0039, 0042) rebase nothing.

patches/0046-surface-picture-swap.diff (X1265 redo, perf track, T1 b305 Settings > Items at rest p95 17.6 ms, all frames
over 8 ms, layout 9-10 ms with 9 views): a playing video layer asked for an animation frame on every display refresh,
and the notify of its view dirtied every ancestor up to the root, so a gift effect at rest rendered, laid out and
painted the window for each picture. PaintSurface carries a swap_key (zero names nothing), set by Surface::swap_key
through Window::paint_swappable_surface and paint_swappable_owned_surface. Window::swap_surface puts a new picture into
every surface of the frame on screen with that key, in the scene and in the paint operations kept for replay, and
asks for a present only; it answers false when the frame holds no such surface (hidden, clipped away, gone). Called
from an on_next_frame callback, a video's next picture costs a present, with no render, layout or paint.

patches/0047-click-notifies-own-view.diff (X1341, perf track, T4 b305 photo opened from a chat p95 34.9-38.9 ms, the
opening frame laid out 149 views: every sheet host, the chat list rows and the hidden feed under the chat): the click
machinery of a div (pending mouse down on press, captured or dropped press on release, the active state on press
and release) called Window::refresh, so every click rendered every cached view of the window. These five spots
now notify the view that painted the element (Window::current_view at paint), which renders it and its ancestors
while the other cached views replay. Drag start and drop keep the refresh: a drag draws outside the view.

patches/0047-path-swap.diff (X1337, perf track, T2 b305 video send in a chat, every upload frame 34-35 views, draw
11-20 ms): the upload ring of a chat media cell asked for an animation frame on every display refresh, and the notify
of the cell dirtied every ancestor up to the chat screen, so a spinning ring rendered, laid out and painted the chat
for each turn. Path carries a swap_key and a swap anchor (moved with a replayed paint), set through
Window::paint_swappable_path; paint_path is that call with key zero, and a path painted under a transformation takes no
key. Window::swap_path lays new geometry, built from the origin, at the anchor of every path of the frame on screen
with that key, in the scene and in the paint operations kept for replay, keeping order, content mask and colour, and
asks for a present only; false when the frame holds no such path. Called from an on_next_frame callback, a turn of
the ring costs a present.

patches/0049-path-swap-colour.diff (X1265, perf track, T1 b329 Settings > Items at rest, 4-6 views, layout 15-23 ms
per frame): the golden sparkles around the photo in the gift shop notified their host 30 times a second, and the
notify dirtied every ancestor up to the root, so each twinkle rendered and laid out the shop sheet and the whole window
under it. A sparkle changes colour (its twinkle) as well as geometry, which Window::swap_path keeps. Path carries the
element opacity it was painted with (swap_opacity); Window::swap_paths lays new geometry and a new colour (times that
opacity) on every path of the frame on screen whose key is in the batch, in one pass over the scene and the paint
operations kept for replay, and asks for a present when every key was found. A twinkle costs a present.

patches/0050-hidden-hitboxes.diff (X1418, T5 b329 Settings: the Moderation row at the bottom of the settings list
answered no click after a visit to another user's profile): a hidden element still prepaints its children, and a
parked cached page under it replays the hitboxes it recorded while shown, at the bounds it had then. An occluding one
blocked whatever is drawn there now. Hitbox carries hidden (hidden_depth > 0 at insert_hitbox or reuse_prepaint) and
the hit test skips it; the bounds stay for the views that read them, and the same range replayed shown is hit again.

patches/0051-dirty-source-origin.diff (X1278, T2 perf logs after 0048): the two biggest dirty_by entries in every
log were relays inside gpui, window.rs request_animation_frame delivering its notify on the next frame and the
use_keyed_state observer notifying the host, so the trace never named who animated or which keyed state dirtied its
host. profiler::with_dirty_origin counts every dirty source noted inside it under a given call site;
request_animation_frame counts its delivered notify once under the requester, use_keyed_state is #[track_caller] and
counts the relayed host notify under its call site. Trace only: no change when frame tracing is off.

patches/0052-tooltip-scroll-cancels-show.diff (X1499, T3 b329: after a wheel scroll of the profile post list the
"Send sparks" label hung at the resting pointer over the next post's video, the button a row higher): a scroll
cleared only a visible tooltip. A show still pending (pointer came to rest on the control less than the show delay
before the scroll) fired after the content had moved, and its visibility check used the bounds of the frame that
scheduled it, so the label stayed. A scroll wheel event now also cancels a pending show; the next pointer move
schedules a fresh one from the current hitbox.

patches/0053-transformed-view-replay.diff (X1475, perf track, T6 b311 4.11.5: Back from a riff to the profile Riffs
grid, the flying page rendered every frame, up to 54 views, p95 9.9-11.9 ms): a cached view painted under
Window::with_transformation replayed the primitives of its last frame as they were, already carrying the old matrix
and clip, so a clean page in a zoom or scale flight had to render each frame or show a frozen frame. The view state
keeps what its paint ran under (PaintContext: matrix, transformation mask, element opacity). When only the matrix and
the clip moved, both scale-and-move matrices, the opacity is the same and the new clip shows nothing the old one cut
away (on screen and through the delta), Window::reuse_transformed_paint replays the range under the new matrix: paths
and transformed sprites take the delta, surfaces their snapped box, every clip becomes the new transformation mask,
layers and untransformed primitives stay. Otherwise the old frame shows once more and the view is notified to render
in the next frame instead of staying frozen. An opacity change alone replays as before.

patches/0054-view-replay-under-moved-mask.diff (X1472, perf track, T3 b331 6.11.27: Profile editor, Choose badge,
the emoji panel revealed by a growing clip, every visible grid row rendered and laid out each spring frame, p95 9.1-9.8
ms): the cache key of a cached view held its content mask exactly, so a parent clip that grew or shrank by a pixel made
every view inside render although none of them was cut. A view whose mask moved now replays when nothing it drew or
hit-tests in the frame just drawn touches the mask it rendered under or the new one (Window::ranges_clear_of_mask with
no offset, strictly inside both). The key keeps the mask the view rendered under, which its recorded primitives carry;
a view cut by either edge renders as before.

patches/0055-mouse-blocker-probe.diff (X1556, T1 b331: the Settings list beside Maps stopped answering wheel and
clicks, reachable=false, until a restart): Window::mouse_blocker_at(position) returns the frontmost hitbox that blocks
the mouse there in the frame on screen (bounds after its content mask, behavior, paint layer, how many plain hitboxes lie
in front), walked in the same paint order as the hit test and skipping hidden ones. A diagnostic only, called from the
X1418 probe of the root list column when a press or a wheel inside it is unreachable; nothing else reads it.

patches/0056-glyph-colour-swap.diff (X1557, T5 b331 4.16.8: riff comments in the side panel, a first comment badge
on screen re-rendered RootView, the side panel and every comment row 30 times a second, p95 14 ms): the badge sweep
recoloured its glyphs through a notify per frame, and a notify dirties every ancestor view. Window::with_glyph_swap_key
marks the glyphs painted inside it with a u32 key (stored in the unused pad of MonochromeSprite and SubpixelSprite, so
no shader or GPU layout changes); Window::swap_glyph_colours recolours every glyph of that key in the frame on screen
(and the copies kept for replay) by its place across the span of the key, keeps its alpha, and presents. False when
the key left the frame.

patches/0058-replayed-hitbox-layer.diff (X1571/X1556, T1 and T2 b331: the Settings column went deaf to wheel and clicks
after the media viewer or a chat with GIFs, reachable=false): reuse_prepaint copied each hitbox with the paint layer it
was recorded on. A cached view first prepainted inside a deferred draw (layer priority + 1) and replayed later in the
root pass kept that layer, so the paint ordered hit test (0032) put it above every root hitbox and it swallowed the
mouse wherever its bounds lay. A replayed hitbox now takes the layer of the pass replaying it; a prepaint range only
ever holds hitboxes of one pass, since deferred draws prepaint in ranges of their own.

patches/0059-transformed-replay-fade.diff (X1275, T6 b311: the gift card sheet opened from a chat rendered both
cosmetic surfaces in every frame of its appearance): the desktop modal appears scaling and fading at once, and the
transformed replay of 0053 refused any change of element opacity, so every cached view inside the modal fell back to
"replay once, notify" and rendered in each frame of the animation. The replay now fades the replayed colours by the
ratio of the opacity now to the opacity painted with (quads, borders, shadows, underlines, paths with their swap
opacity, glyph and image sprites; a surface carries no element opacity). A paint at zero opacity still renders: it
dropped its transparent primitives, so a fade cannot bring them back.

patches/0060-emoji-tile-prewarm.diff (X1616, perf track, T6 b331 14.8.3: wheel scroll of the Emoji tab in the chat
input panel, p95 110-122 ms with only 23 views, paint 75-98 ms of it): every colour emoji a wheel step revealed was
rasterized by CoreText inside the paint of that frame (Window::paint_emoji fills the sprite atlas on a miss), close to
a hundred per step. TextSystem::rasterize_emoji_text shapes a string and rasterizes its distinct emoji glyphs with the
params paint_emoji uses; Window::prewarm_emoji_tiles runs it on the background executor and inserts the tiles into the
window's atlas on the foreground, without a notify. The grid warms the rows ahead of its scroll position, so the paint
of a wheel step finds its tiles ready.

patches/0061-moved-replay-reshaped-mask.diff (X1629, perf track, PERF bench b338 profile p50 4.6 -> 6.7 ms: opening a
profile pushed the page into the clipped centre column, and every visible ProfileGridPostCellView rendered in each
frame of the slide, ~20 a frame, 8 ms frames): a 0041 moved replay took a mask that moved along or stayed, but a page
sliding into a column clips its rows by the intersection of its own clip (moving) and the column's (fixed), so the
mask grew in every frame and every cached row of the page rendered. A view whose mask changed shape now replays moved
when nothing it drew or hit-tests in the frame just drawn touches the mask it rendered under, nor touches the new
mask after the move (Window::ranges_clear_of_mask with and without the offset); the recorded clips move with it and
still cut nothing. Rows cut by the column edge render as before.

patches/0062-rendering-view.diff (X1265, perf track, T4 b338: Settings > Items shop, the whole grid of 135 views
rendered in single frames for 7-10 s after opening): every mark of a Sai slice (pending, fulfilled, rejected) ran

records its readers on read and notifies only them.

patches/0063-nested-paint-rebase.diff (X1284, perf track, T1 b338: Settings > Customization > Chat wallpapers, every
preset tap rendered all wallpaper tiles and switches of the page): 0045 rebased the prepaint of cached views nested in
a view that replayed, but left their paint range and painted_frame, so after any frame in which the page replayed

the frame just before and prepainted in this one (PaintIndex::rebase_within, Window::update_replayed_paint_states).
Moved and transformed replays leave nested views as before.

patches/0064-tooltip-show-notifies-view.diff (X1641, perf track, T7 b338: Profile, badge picker opened twice in a
row, every badge hover label redrew the whole post grid): a tooltip that finished its show delay called

patches/0065-faded-replay.diff (X1624, T3 b331: group Permissions, the switches of the rows revealed under
"Send photos and videos" stayed invisible until a click): a cached view replaying in place ignored the element
opacity (PaintContext::places_alike sets it aside), so a view first painted inside a fade-in kept that faint frame
for good. An in-place replay under another opacity now fades the replayed colours by the ratio
(Window::reuse_faded_paint, PaintReplay::Faded, Scene::replay_faded over the 0059 Primitive::fade); from or to zero
opacity it shows the old frame once and renders in the next one. A moved replay under another opacity also renders
in the next frame. Faded replays leave nested cached views unrebased, as moved and transformed ones do.

patches/0066-move-and-deactivate-no-refresh.diff (X1553, T1 b331: tab Posts drew frames of 102 views,
26-44 ms, without input): Window::bounds_changed refreshed the whole window on every move and on every
activation change, so each cached view rendered again. It now refreshes only when the content size, the
scale factor or the display changes; bounds observers still run on every call. A window that loses
activation is no longer refreshed (activation observers still run and notify what they need); a window
that becomes active is refreshed as before, since animated images request frames only while active.

patches/0068-retained-line-layouts.diff (X1616, perf track, T6b b344: chat input > Emoji tab, wheel steps of 38 ms
with layout 35 ms and 19 views): each plain emoji cell is its own text line, and the layout that first showed a row
shaped every new cell through CoreText on the main thread. LineLayoutCache keeps a retained map across frames, filled
off the main thread by LineLayoutRetainer::retain (WindowTextSystem::line_layout_retainer,
Window::prewarm_line_layouts); layout_line reads it after the current and previous frames and before shaping. Only
single-run lines without force_width; the map is cleared at 16384 lines.

patches/0070-cache-miss-reasons.diff (X1275, perf track, T6b b344: a gift card opened from a chat, every chat list

failed check of the in-place replay (dirty, refresh, size, origin, mask, text_style, env, prepaint_gap,
dropped_deferred, stale_hidden, paint_gap; new without a state), profiler::note_cache_miss hands it to the render
that follows, cache_miss_counts sums it per Render type. No-op unless frame tracing is enabled. The app writes it
as the miss_by line of the perf log.

patches/0072-image-fade-swap.diff (X1674, perf track, T2 b344: chat profile opened on the right with tab Items, p95

patches/0073-moved-nested-rebase.diff (X1343, perf track, T3 b351: gift wardrobe Avatar frame, wheel scroll p95 9-10 ms,

outer mask moved along, is taken when the outer mask stayed and was the nested one, else the nested view renders as
before. The moved paint branch rebases the nested paints as 0063 does. A nested view that listens to the mouse is
marked moved (0044).

patches/0074-wholly-hidden-renders-on-reveal.diff (X1277, T6 b351: Items grid cells black after scroll and on tab open):

patches/0078-glyph-visibility-swap.diff (X1707 redo, perf track, T1 b351 8.16.1: holding the microphone in a chat

patches/0079-glyph-shift-swap.diff (X1754, perf track, T4 b351 15.25.2: the Music tab drew a frame of 220-290 ms

kept while their clip hides them (line paint and Scene::insert_primitive skip the cull, ordered by the clip), so the
overflowing tail slides in. None when the key left the frame; Some(false) when moved but clipped out before and after.

patches/0083-parked-paint-context.diff (X1769, T1 b351: Posts after the Sai debugger and Settings, one feed row

patches/0084-shift-group.diff (X1796, perf track, T5 b359: opening a journey with photo pins rendered MapJourneyPage on
24-28 of 28-33 frames of the camera fit): a pin sits at a projected spot, so each camera frame notified the map surface,
and gpui dirtied the page and every ancestor up to the root. Window::with_shift_group(key, f) names the paint operations
f paints; Window::shift_group(key, offset) moves their primitives (all kinds, clip included, as a moved replay) in the
frame on screen and presents. The copies kept for replay stay where they were painted (the group remembers how far the
copies on screen moved), so a later moved replay still starts from the painted spot. Hitboxes stay; the caller renders
once the motion ends. False when the key left the frame (a cached ancestor replayed whole records no group) or a
primitive was not found on screen; the caller then renders.

patches/0088-spliced-holes.diff (X1835, perf track, T2 b361 X1682: a notify inside the chat screen rendered every view up
to RootView and laid out the window, 8 views, layout 9-12 ms, frame 16-19 ms): when only cached views changed, the frame
is spliced: the frame just drawn is copied in spans around the outermost notified cached views (prepaint and paint
ranges, dispatch path left open by DispatchTree::reuse_span/finish_spans) and each of them is drawn alone at its old
bounds under the stacks recorded when it was drawn (HoleRecord/HoleStacks in Frame::holes, captured in ViewElement
prepaint and paint). No root render, no window layout. Refused (plain draw) on refresh, a11y, prompt, drag, inspector,
deferred draws or tooltips in the last frame, a viewport change, a notified view without a hole record, or a hole whose
style no longer gives its old size. Copied cached views get their ranges rebased (rebase_spliced_views, SpliceMap).
App::detect_own_accessed_entities keeps what a cached view read itself (Frame::own_reads) apart from what the cached views
inside it read, so a store read only by an inner view makes only that one a hole. An environment kept in an App global
(rise-ui env_scope) is restored through EnvSnapshotHooks (set_env_snapshot_hooks); without hooks a view drawn under a
non-zero env fingerprint is never a hole.

patches/0089-partly-culled-reveal.diff (X1876, T7 b361: Moderation > Reports, oldest first, the tenth row stayed a blank
strip after scrolling, its separator and press shown): Scene::insert_primitive drops a primitive its clip cuts away

patches/0094-shape-outside-lock.diff (X1563, perf track: a feed scroll frame spent 80.7 ms shaping five short row

patches/0092-frame-thread-cpu.diff (X1779, perf track: the tabs bench kept one 38-48 ms frame per run whose views,

patches/0096-stale-paint-range.diff (X1986, crash: closing the Buy item gift shop sheet from My Sparks aborted the app in

logs "gpui 0096 stale paint range" with the source (view or deferred), the view type and both lengths, so the replay

patches/0098-spliced-deferred-draws.diff (X1987, perf track, T4 b387/390 X1679: any notify inside an open sheet, popover
or modal, all drawn through deferred(), rendered MusicLibraryView, MainTabComponentPage and RootView and laid out the
window: 0088 refused every frame that followed a frame with a deferred draw, splice outcome unspliceable): a frame with
deferred draws may be spliced. Each hole lies in the root pass or inside the ranges of one deferred draw of the frame
just drawn (HolePass), and that pass is copied in spans around its holes the same way (splice_prepaint_pass,
splice_paint_pass). A span copies the deferred draws it registered (element None, DeferredDraw::copied_from = index in
the frame just drawn, parent node through SpliceNodes, the old to new dispatch node map of all copied spans); the
deferred pass then replays a copied draw whole as before, or splices it when it holds holes, in the same rounds and
priority order; a hole that registers deferred draws draws them fresh. A deferred pass copies its dispatch nodes under
the draw's parent (SpliceSpans::with_base). SpliceMap keeps one SplicePass per pass (segments and holes; a draw
replayed whole is one segment), so hole records and cached views of every pass are rebased. Refused with pass:<view
type> when a hole lies in no pass, with order when the deferred draw holding a hole is not copied (registered inside
another hole). Tooltips, prompts, drags and the inspector still refuse. A notified view that is not a cached view is
still no_hole: the view that changes inside a sheet must be cached to be drawn alone.

patches/0099-relative-clips.diff (X2003, perf track: X1277 Items grid p95 13 with 35-48 ms row entries, X1579 GIF

transformations and hole stacks) gives the clips primitives keep (snapped_content_mask, paths, paint_layer, the
glyph cull in line.rs), and the scene draws each primitive cut by the clip stack while the paint operations keep it
as painted, even cut away whole (order and path id copied back). Replays move PushClip with the view, so the clips
around stay those of the frame. A view whose range was recorded so (ViewElementState::relative_clips) skips the
culled and wholly_hidden refusals and replays moved where the mask cut it; reuse_moved_prepaint reopens each hitbox
mask on the edges the old outer mask drew and cuts it by the new one. Content masks for hit tests and cache keys
stay the window's (content_mask). A spliced hole (0088) reopens no boundary: its paint stacks carry it
(own_clip_boundary, hole_clip_boundary). A shift group (0084) keeps the clip around it fixed. Glyph culling inside
a cell stops at its own clips, so a long row half on screen shapes all its glyphs once.

patches/0100-spliced-layout-states.diff (X2004, perf track, b395 T1 at idle: 150 frames a second, 100% CPU, every
window of the testers; root, root, spliced in a loop from the launch on, sheet host coordinators, keyed states and
cached view states built anew in each round): a spliced frame (0088) listed the element state keys of the copied
prepaint spans only, from the root prepaint on, and dropped every state the root layout had read before it (render of
RootView and of every view and component rendered outside a cached view: use_keyed_state, on_change slots). The
next root render found them gone, so appear, change and coordinator handlers notified, and the splice after that
dropped them again. With deferred draws spliced since 0098, the launch logo's frames spliced and the loop never
ended. Window::splice_frame now lists the keys the frame just drawn read before its root prepaint first, so the
states of the layout that is not run again carry over unchanged.

patches/0101-replay-clip.diff (X2005, after 0099): a cached view painted inside its clip boundary keeps primitives
with masks relative to it (relative_clips). Replayed where no boundary opens (under a transformation, where
begin_clip_boundary refuses), the in-place, moved or parked replay inserted them with no clip, so a row spilled
out of the scroll mask. Window::begin_replay_clip now pushes a scene clip of the mask around the view
(content_mask, window coordinates under a transformation) around such a replay, and end_replay_clip pops it;
relative_clips stays set for the copied range.

patches/0104-transformed-inner-clips.diff (X2014): under Window::with_transformation the content mask stays the one
active when it was pushed, so masks pushed inside (a scroll clip, a sheet surface) cut nothing and the share sheet
rows spilled below the sheet while it scaled in. with_content_mask now also pushes a scene clip of the mask mapped
through the matrix when it only scales and moves (transformed_mask_clip); layout and hit testing keep the
untransformed masks. Scene::replay_transformed maps a recorded clip through the delta (TransformedReplay::follow_clip)
inside the new mask instead of widening it to that mask. A cached view painted under a transformation records no
splice hole: drawn alone after the modal came to rest it painted again under the stale matrix and its masks, so the
rows stayed spilled at rest.

patches/0106-hidden-nested-rebase.diff (X1370): a cached view that replays moved (0073) also rebases a nested
cached view that showed nothing before and shows nothing after under the new outer mask (a grid cell of an off-screen
pager page under its own scroll clip), moving its own mask along, as the 0067 replay of the view itself would. Before,
such cells kept the ranges of their last render, were a frame behind (origin:gap) and all rendered on the next render
of their page: 30 story cells and 26-30 ms frames on each Comments/Reposts switch of the profile.

patches/0107-stale-click-capture.diff (X2153): a mouse up whose bubble an inner element stopped (a plain button
inside a clickable row: the post header's music line inside the author column) left the outer element's
captured_mouse_down set, since only its bubble clears it. The outer row then fired its click on the next mouse up
anywhere its cached listeners were replayed (the back button over the sound page opened the author's profile in the
panel). The capture phase now clears the captured press before taking a fresh one.

patches/0108-deferred-draw-reads.diff (X1444): a deferred element lays out in prepaint_deferred_draws, after the
view that deferred it was drawn, so whatever it read there (the lazy rows of a list inside a sheet, the story rings and
pagination states they read) ran outside every capture and became a direct read of the frame: each notify of such a
store dirtied the root and forced a full draw. The deferred prepaint now runs inside detect_own_accessed_entities and
its reads go to the cached view that deferred it (own_reads merged, a cached_views entry with the full set), kept on
the DeferredDraw so a replayed or spliced draw still names them. A draw deferred by the root keeps the old direct
reads.

patches/0109-nested-replay-readers.diff (X2223): a cached view replayed inside its replayed ancestor (0045 rebase,
0073 moved rebase) took its new ranges but never entered cached_views or own_reads of the frame, so it was no reader
of what it read. A notify of such a store dirtied only the ancestor (its full reads hold the nested ones), which
rendered and replayed the nested view on its stale frame: the post composer hero kept its loading spinner after the
decoded preview landed, until a page switch notified the page again. The nested rebase now registers the view with
its accessed and own entities, as its own replay does; update_replayed_states passes the element key along.

patches/0110-backdrop-blur.diff (X2270): gpui had no backdrop filter, so the list headers could only tint the rows
scrolled under them. BorderStyle::BackdropBlur marks a quad that blurs what is drawn under it before its own
background: border_widths.top is the gaussian sigma, border_widths.bottom the strip at the bottom where the blur thins
out to none (smoothstep), border_color transparent; Window::paint_backdrop_blur paints one, and paint_quad keeps it
whole even with no tint. The Metal renderer ends the pass at such a quad, blurs across from the drawable into a
viewport sized scratch texture and down back onto the drawable inside the rounded bounds and content mask, then goes
on. The drawable must be readable: the first blur of a window turns framebuffer_only off on its layer, that frame goes
without the blur. wgpu and DirectX draw the quad as an ordinary one (its background only); BACKDROP_BLUR_SUPPORTED
tells the caller. Replays, fades, moves and shift groups treat it as any quad.

patches/0112-motion-group.diff (X1713): a shift group (0084) could only move. Window::move_group shows a group scaled by
`scale`, moved by `translation` and faded by `fade` against the paint kept for replay (a point painted at p lands at
p * scale + translation), clips kept where they were painted, so every call starts from the paint and a fade back
from zero still finds its colours. Scaling takes paths and transformed sprites (what a paint under a transformation
records); anything else refuses and the caller renders. Scene::replay of a whole cached view in place now carries
its shift groups and shows them where they were moved, so an ancestor redrawing around a moving row neither snaps
it back nor makes the next move refuse; replays at another origin or opacity still drop them. The forum rail rides
the chat rows on it: an open moves avatars and fades bodies without rendering the rows.

patches/0114-progressive-backdrop-blur.diff (X2362): the 0110 blur had one sigma over the whole quad and only thinned its
alpha at the bottom, so an edge band read as an evenly frosted strip. Window::paint_progressive_backdrop_blur marks the
quad's left (from the top) or right (from the bottom) border; the Metal shader then gives every row its own sigma: full
over the first `hold` (border_widths.bottom) from that edge, smoothstep down to none at the opposite edge. Both passes
take the sigma of the row they draw, so the cost stays two passes; rows under a third of a pixel copy the source.

patches/0115-ease-in-progressive-blur.diff (X2370): the owner found the 0114 edge blur too short and too abrupt from weak
to strong. The progressive sigma now falls as an ease in seen from the content side, 1 - cos(u * pi / 2), u from 0 at
the far edge to 1 at the held band: it starts unnoticeably at the content and keeps growing up to the edge.

patches/0116-list-paint-under-top-padding.diff (X2370): a list with a top padding painted nothing above its scroll top
item, so content laid under a translucent header over the padding ended at the padding. ListState::paint_under_top_padding
(off by default) renders the items above the scroll top into the part of the padding the scroll top item leaves
uncovered and places them above it, so the rows scroll on under the header (emoji and sticker picker pack strip).

patches/0117-owned-surface-device-size.diff (Linux and Windows build): the off macOS arm of the surface element (0001)
passed the owned frame size in logical pixels to ObjectFit::get_bounds, which takes the image size in device pixels, so
gpui did not compile for any target but macOS. The frame width and height now go in as DevicePixels, as the macOS arm does.

patches/0128-deferred-image-drops.diff (macOS crash in MetalAtlas::metal_texture): Window::drop_image freed atlas tiles
at once, while the frame on screen could still draw them; gpui presents that frame again without a draw while input
runs fast (typing), so a texture freed in between (the app frees unheld images every 2 s) aborted render_frame on an
unwrap. drop_image now queues the keys and the next Window::draw removes them before it paints (at most 4096 wait), and
the Metal, wgpu and DirectX renderers skip a sprite batch whose texture is gone instead of panicking.

patches/0129-wheel-into-children.diff (#160, a width capped column scrolls from its margins): InteractiveElement::wheel_into_children
gives the element a hitbox that keeps the area of its children (Hitbox::wheel_area, relative to the hitbox, so a replayed
hitbox keeps it). A ScrollWheelEvent whose front-most such hitbox has the pointer outside that area is dispatched at the
nearest point of the area (at least 24 px in from its side edges) with the hit test of that point, so the scroll views,
lists and gesture gates of the column handle it as if the pointer were over them; nested columns follow up to 4 hops.
The real hit test and pointer position are restored right after, so hover and cursor do not move.

patches/0130-windows-virtual-file-drop.diff (#180, Windows drag and drop): the OLE drop target took only CF_HDROP, so
an image dragged from a browser, mail client or messenger (virtual files: FileGroupDescriptorW plus FileContents per
item, no CF_HDROP) got DROPEFFECT_NONE and nothing happened. DragEnter now reads only the descriptors and enters the
drag with the paths the items will have under %TEMP%\riseonly-drop\<stamp>\; Drop streams each item's contents
(HGLOBAL block or IStream in 64 KiB chunks, never the whole file in memory) into those paths before the drop is
submitted, and removes riseonly-drop folders older than a day. Folders and unreadable items leave no file. DragOver
and Drop answer DROPEFFECT_NONE when DragEnter found nothing to drop.

patches/0131-windows-bundled-color-font-fallback.diff (#181, the Windows emoji set): DirectWrite fallback only looked
families up in the system collection, so a color font the app added with add_fonts was never used for characters the
primary font lacks; emoji always came from Segoe UI Emoji. add_fonts now records every color (COLR) face of the custom
collection with its Unicode ranges, and each font's fallback maps those ranges to that family in the custom collection
ahead of the requested fallbacks and the system fallback. Without a bundled color font nothing changes.
